::: {.callout-warning}
## Before you leave it running overnight

This experiment leaves a board, a host computer and (if used) a mains-powered
insulated enclosure running, unattended, for over 24 hours. That is not a
detail — it is the one thing about T3 that is different from every earlier
experiment on this site, and it carries its own risks:

- **Fire and overheating.** Any mains-powered heater, incubator or heat mat
  used to add a small controlled offset must be rated for continuous
  unattended operation, fused appropriately, and placed on a
  non-flammable surface away from anything that can fall onto it. If in doubt,
  do not add active heating — an insulated box at ambient temperature is a
  perfectly good T3 rig on its own.
- **The host must be allowed to stay on.** Disable automatic sleep, suspend
  and unattended OS updates that could reboot the machine mid-run; a
  restart part-way through the log is a lost 24 hours, not a recoverable
  error.
- **Tell people it is running.** A board and a host left on a bench overnight
  in a shared space should be labelled with what it is, when it started, when
  it is expected to finish, and a contact — so nobody unplugs it, moves it, or
  "helpfully" shuts it down.
- **Check it before you leave, and as soon as you are back.** Confirm the
  stream has actually started and is writing records before you walk away;
  confirm it is still running, and did not silently stop hours ago, before
  you trust the file at the end.
:::

### 1. Build the insulated box {#sec-t3-step-box}

Any enclosure that meaningfully slows heat exchange with the room works:
a cooler box, an expanded-polystyrene box, or several layers of insulating
foam around the sensor. There is no fixed design here — what matters is that
the box's own time constant is long compared with the room's own temperature
fluctuations on the timescale of minutes, not that it reaches any particular
insulation figure.

Mount the sensor near the centre of the enclosed volume, away from the walls
and away from any electronics inside the box that could add its own
self-heating (@doebelin) close to the sensing element.

### 2. Identify the board and the host {#sec-t3-step-identify}

```bash
arduino-io list
arduino-io info
```

As in every other experiment, write `board.adc_bits`, `board.vref_mV` and the
firmware version into the sidecar. T3 additionally needs the **host**
confirmed as one that will stay powered and awake for the whole run — see the
callout above.

### 3. Start the log {#sec-t3-step-start}

A sample every few seconds is plenty; there is no dynamic content in this
signal, only a slow drift and a slower diurnal cycle, and a fast sampling
rate only makes the file larger for no benefit:

```bash
arduino-io mode 15 analog
arduino-io stream 15 --hz 0.2 --seconds 86400 --csv data/log-24h.csv
```

`--hz 0.2` is one sample every 5 seconds; adjust to match the sensor and
board actually in use, and record whatever period was actually used in the
sidecar's `acquisition.requested_period_us`.

### 4. Watch it start, then leave it {#sec-t3-step-watch}

Confirm the first few records are landing before you walk away — a stream
that fails to start looks, from across the room, identical to one that is
quietly logging 24 hours of nothing. Check back periodically if that is
practical; do not adjust the box, the sensor or its wiring while it is
running, since any disturbance shows up in the record indistinguishable from
a real event.

### 5. Recover and close out the run {#sec-t3-step-recover}

After at least 24 hours, stop the stream, copy the full summary line into
`stream_stats`, and inspect the record before doing anything else: plot it
raw, and confirm there are no obvious gaps, resets or a truncated final
segment. A run that stopped early is still useful, but it must be labelled as
shorter than 24 hours, not padded or extrapolated to look like one that
finished.

### 6. Fill the sidecar {#sec-t3-step-sidecar}

- [ ] `board.adc_bits`, `board.vref_mV` — from `arduino-io info`
- [ ] `host.os`, `host.machine` — the host that stayed on, and whether it was
      ever asleep or restarted during the run (if it was, say so; do not
      silently ship a discontinuous record as if it were continuous)
- [ ] `acquisition.requested_period_us` **and** `acquisition.achieved_rate_hz`
- [ ] all six `stream_stats` counters
- [ ] `environment.notes` — what the insulation was, roughly how the box was
      built, and anything unusual overnight (a door left open nearby, a
      heating system cycling, direct sun reaching the bench)
- [ ] `synthetic: false`
